scams.name: Great Barrier Reef 'Cheap Day Tour' Bait & Switch
scams.description: You walk down the Esplanade past a rack of brochures and a friendly agent offers a Great Barrier Reef full day at $99 — 'same tour, way cheaper than the bigger operators.' You book, pay cash. On the morning of the trip the boat heads to Green Island (an inner-reef sandspit tourists have been visiting since the 1890s), where visibility is 3–5 metres, coral cover is limited, and the reef-pontoon lunch is an up-sell. The outer-reef tours you thought you booked are at sites 90 minutes further offshore.
scams.avoidance: The fix is to book directly with outer-reef certified operators. Passions of Paradise (sailing day trip to outer Michaelmas Cay and Paradise Reef), Silverswift (high-speed catamaran to three outer-reef sites), Sunlover (reef pontoon at Moore Reef), Quicksilver (from Port Douglas to Agincourt Ribbon Reefs), and Ocean Freedom (small-group Upolu Cay) are the legitimate operators. Expect to pay $220–$300 for a full day including lunch and snorkel gear — this is what a real outer-reef trip costs. If an offer is $99 all-in, you are booking an inner-reef or half-day coastal tour. Book direct with Passions of Paradise, Silverswift, Sunlover, Quicksilver, Reef Magic, or Ocean Freedom; Ask the specific outer-reef site name (e.g. Michaelmas Cay, Flynn Reef, Agincourt Ribbon #4); Pay by credit card for chargeback protection; Check the operator is listed at tourismtropicalnq.com.au or has a Queensland ABN; Read the 50 most recent TripAdvisor reviews before booking — fake sites have reviews dated clumped together
scams.location: Cairns Reef Fleet Terminal (Spence Street), booking booths on the Esplanade

scams.name: Backpacker Hostel / Sharehouse Prepayment Scam
scams.description: You've just landed in Cairns on a Working Holiday Visa and you're looking for a cheap sharehouse to settle for a couple of months. On a Facebook backpacker group a 'landlord' offers a room in Edge Hill for $190/week — bank-transfer two weeks' deposit to secure it. You send $380. When you arrive at the address, the house is someone else's home, the Facebook account is deactivated, and your money is gone.
scams.avoidance: Your rule of thumb: never pay before you see the room. Verified Cairns hostels (Gilligan's, Tropic Days, Calypso, Travellers Oasis, Nomads) take payment at check-in or through HostelWorld/Booking.com with platform protection. For sharehouses, insist on an in-person viewing and meet the other housemates. Pay rent only after you have keys and the room is as advertised. The WHV community around Cairns is tight-knit — ask in r/Cairns or the Cairns Backpackers Facebook group before transferring to any 'landlord' you haven't met. Never pay before an in-person viewing — inspect the room and meet current housemates; Book hostels only via HostelWorld, Booking.com, Hostelz or directly at the hostel reception; For sharehouses, pay the first week only after you have keys and have moved in; Ask in r/Cairns or the Cairns Backpackers Facebook group for verified current sharehouses; If scammed, file a report with QLD Police via police.qld.gov.au/online-reporting for insurance
scams.location: Advertised via Facebook backpacker groups, Gumtree, Airbnb clones — targeting WHV workers

scams.name: Cairns Airport / 13cabs Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: You land at Cairns Airport late in the evening and grab a cab at the rank for the five-minute ride to your Esplanade hotel. The meter appears to skip numbers, there's a 'night surcharge' you weren't warned about, and the driver demands $62 for what Google Maps says is a $14 trip. You pay because you want to get to bed.
scams.avoidance: Your fix is Uber or DiDi from Cairns Airport, both of which operate legitimately with pickup at the designated rideshare bay. The standard fare from CNS to the Esplanade is $18–$25 on Uber. If you must use a taxi, insist on meter payment before leaving the curb, and pay by card on the in-car terminal (never hand over your physical card). Sunbus runs the 110 bus from the airport to the CBD roughly hourly for $2.40 during peak — the cheapest option. For the Reef Fleet Terminal to airport direction, pre-book with the hotel concierge or a transfer service like Cairns Airport Shuttles. Use Uber or DiDi from Cairns Airport — standard fare to Esplanade is $18–$25; Take Sunbus route 110 from the airport to the CBD if travelling light ($2.40, roughly hourly); Insist on the meter running before the taxi pulls away; Pay by card on the in-car terminal and screenshot the receipt; If overcharged, photograph the taxi plate and file a complaint with Taxi Services Commission QLD
scams.location: Cairns Airport arrivals, Reef Fleet Terminal drop-off, CBD Esplanade ranks

scams.name: Rental Car Phantom Damage Charge (FNQ Drives)
scams.description: You pick up a Toyota RAV4 from a major rental chain at Cairns Airport, drive the Captain Cook Highway to Port Douglas, Cape Tribulation and back — a classic FNQ self-drive. You return the car with no issues. Three weeks later a $1,900 AUD charge appears on your credit card: 'undercarriage damage' the desk agent 'didn't notice' at drop-off.
scams.avoidance: Your defence is aggressive video documentation. Before driving off the rental lot at Cairns Airport, film every panel, the undercarriage (drop the phone camera), the interior, the odometer reading, the fuel level, and every existing scratch or dent. Repeat the process at drop-off with the desk agent visible in the video, and request a signed no-damage receipt before you leave. Pay with a credit card that provides primary CDW insurance (Amex Platinum, Chase Sapphire Reserve, Capital One Venture X) so you can chargeback. Do not drive rental vehicles on Bloomfield Track or any unsealed road — the rental contract explicitly voids insurance, and any subsequent damage claim will be yours alone. Film the car thoroughly at pickup AND drop-off — all sides, underneath, interior, odometer, fuel; Request a signed no-damage receipt before leaving the drop-off — photograph it in the agent's hand; Pay with a credit card that covers primary CDW (Amex Platinum, Chase Sapphire Reserve); Do not drive rental cars on Bloomfield Track or any unsealed Cape Tribulation north road — insurance is void; If a surprise invoice appears, chargeback immediately and report to Consumer Affairs QLD
scams.location: Cairns Airport, Cairns CBD rental depots — especially for Cape Tribulation and Undara self-drives

scams.name: Fake Daintree / Cape Tribulation Day Tour Booking
scams.description: You Google 'Daintree Rainforest day tour' and a sleek site appears near the top ad slot — $89 all-inclusive, pickup from your Cairns hotel. You book, receive a PDF confirmation with what looks like legitimate Queensland Tourism branding. On tour day, no bus arrives. The phone number rings dead. The confirmation 'operator' doesn't exist in any Australian Business Register.
scams.avoidance: The safe pattern is to book Daintree and Cape Tribulation tours through established FNQ operators with physical offices or verified Queensland Tourism endorsements: Billy Tea Safaris (billyteasafaris.com.au), Down Under Tours, Tropical Horizons Tours, and Daintree Ecotours. Cross-check the operator's ABN at abn.business.gov.au — every legitimate Australian tour operator is ABN-registered. Pay by credit card for chargeback protection. If you prefer to book through a marketplace, Viator and GetYourGuide vet operators more aggressively than random Google results. Book through Billy Tea Safaris, Down Under Tours, Tropical Horizons, Daintree Ecotours, or Viator/GetYourGuide; Verify ABN at abn.business.gov.au and physical address on Google Maps; Pay by credit card for chargeback protection — never bank transfer or PayPal F&F; Read TripAdvisor reviews from the last 6 months for reality checks; Confirm pickup by email and phone the day before — silent operators are red flags
scams.location: Online booking sites, Google Ads, Facebook Ads targeting Cairns visitors

scams.name: Fake Short-Stay Apartment Listing (Esplanade / Palm Cove)
scams.description: You find a 'Coral Sea view apartment' in Palm Cove on a professional-looking site for $160/night — beautiful photos, a polite host, bank-transfer requested because 'Airbnb fees inflate the price.' You send $1,120 for a week. When you arrive, the address is an occupied family home. The site has been taken down. The emails bounce.
scams.avoidance: Your defence is the same as anywhere: book through airbnb.com or booking.com directly, use the app or a bookmarked URL, never pay by bank transfer outside the platform. Reverse image-search listing photos in Google Images; fake listings almost always reuse real-estate marketing shots. Check for reviews from multiple guests in the past 12 months. Ask for a live 60-second video call if any detail feels off. Cairns-specific: confirm the property is in the right location using Google Street View — Palm Cove is 27 km north of the Esplanade, not walking distance as some scam listings imply. Book only through airbnb.com or booking.com via the app or a bookmarked URL; Never pay by bank transfer outside the platform — escrow is the whole point; Reverse image-search the photos in Google Images; Check the property address against Google Street View — match the location; Require reviews from 3+ guests in the past year
scams.location: Cairns Esplanade, Palm Cove, Trinity Beach — Airbnb / Booking.com clone sites
